---
title: "03_contrast_analysis"
output: html_document
---

Purpose: process the stage 1 contrast models (`02_contrast_modeling.qmd`, one model per species
and variant) into per-species summaries of the subadult - adult contrast and how consistent it
is across sites, years and events, check them against the unified model (m11g), and export the
contrasts for stage 2. Questions Q1-Q6 and definitions: `README.md`.

Scales used throughout:

- **prevalence part**: contrasts on the **logit prevalence** scale (= -logit(hu), the sign of the
  hu coefficients flipped), so a positive contrast means subadults are *more often infected*.
  Also shown as a difference in percentage points at a typical site and year.
- **load part**: differences in mu (mean log Bd load density among positive swabs). Positive =
  subadults carry *higher loads when infected*. Also shown as a fold difference (exp).
- Contrasts are compared within species only (labs differ in absolute levels).

What each summary means:

- **mean contrast** (Q1): the `stage_c` coefficient. stage_c = -0.5 / +0.5, so the coefficient is
  the full subadult - adult difference at a typical site, year and event.
- **contrast sd** per level (Q2-Q4): how much the contrast varies between sites, site-years
  (within sites) or events (within site-years). Only levels allowed by the species' tier have one.
  Tier **D** parts have none: one mean contrast, and consistency is "not estimable". The reason
  is recorded: *few co-sampled sites* (< 3; the mean mostly reflects those sites) or
  *between-population* (< 25% of swabs in co-sampled sites; the mean mostly compares different
  populations). A tier D interval covers the sampled sites only, so it is narrower than a
  species-wide one. Levels a part cannot separate (R2) and sigma structure (R3) are recorded in
  the job table (README "Contrast levels", "Nuisance structure").
- **contraction**: 1 - posterior variance / prior variance of a contrast sd. Near 1: the data
  pinned it down. Near 0: the posterior is still the prior (not informed; expected where few
  units are co-sampled). Used to fade out uninformed levels, not as a test.
- **sign consistency** per level: the probability that a new site (site-year, event) has a
  contrast with the same sign as the mean, = Phi(|mean| / sd), computed per draw. "all levels"
  combines every modeled level: a new event in a new year at a new site. It reads the sd on the
  scale of the mean: sd 0.4 around a mean of 1 is consistent, around a mean of 0.1 it is not.
- **variance shares** (Q5): sd^2 of a level / the sum over modeled levels. Comparable only between
  species with the same tier.
- **stage levels**: each stage's prevalence (%) or median load among positives at a typical site,
  year and event: what the contrast is a difference of. Within-species context only (labs
  differ).
- **intercept**: a unit's overall infection, the midpoint of the two stages (prevalence on the
  logit scale, signed so higher = more prevalent; load on log load among positives). Intercepts
  vary at every level in every tier and are informed by every unit, not just co-sampled ones.
- **intercept-contrast correlation** (Q6): do sites (years, events) with more Bd overall have a
  larger contrast? Estimated by the model at each level with a contrast slope.
- **sd ratio**: contrast sd / intercept sd at a level. < 1 = the gap varies less than overall
  infection does there.
- **group contrasts**: each population's (site-year's, event's) contrast = mean + its deviations
  down the hierarchy. Groups where both stages were not co-sampled are shrunk toward their parent
  and are marked, so they are not read as observed contrasts.
- **flag** (a caveat label per species and part; it does not change the model):
  *between-population* = a tier D part whose species has < 25% of swabs in co-sampled sites;
  *time-segregated* = fewer co-sampled events than half the number of co-sampled site-years (no
  minimum number of site-years since 2026-11-26), so the contrast partly compares different
  times of year. Computed in `01_contrast_tiers.Rmd` and read from the job table. A
  time-segregated species can also be tier D (*few co-sampled sites*, e.g. *L. blairi*); the
  plots show the flag and the tier together. A low event count can also come from small events
  (< 5 swabs of a stage per survey run) rather than different times: README "Definitions".

Run order: `01_contrast_tiers.Rmd` (job table), cluster fits copied into
`size_bd_contrast/models/`, `02_contrast_modeling.qmd` (full model checks), then this script.
Optional comparisons read `size_bd_unified/intermediates/unified_03_b_spp_lss_draws.parquet`
(m11g) and `size_bd_season/intermediates/03_all_contrast_summary.csv` (seasonal models).

# Setup
```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

# setup
librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, brms, posterior, patchwork, arrow, ggrepel)

models_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "models")
figures_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "figures")
intermediates_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "intermediates")
dir.create(figures_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# model data (brms_data), created by size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd
load(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "bd_model_env_unified_2026-11-12.RData"))

# add_contrast_groups, co_unit_flags, constants
source(here("size_bd_contrast", "contrast_data_functions.R"))
# contrast_slope_groups, contrast_sd_prior_quantile
source(here("size_bd_contrast", "contrast_model_functions.R"))
# conv_check
source(here("size_bd_season", "season_check_functions.R"))
# f_draw_agg: median / 50% / 95% intervals, net effect, pd and support labels, so contrasts are
# reported in the same language as the unified analysis
source(here("size_bd_unified", "contrast_functions.R"))

```

# Jobs and fits
```{r}
contrast_jobs = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_contrast_jobs.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(job = paste(taxon_capture, variant, sep = "_"))

model_files = set_names(file.path(models_dir, paste0("size_bd_contrast_model_zln_c1_", contrast_jobs$job, ".rds")),
                        contrast_jobs$job)

missing_fits = names(model_files)[!file.exists(model_files)]
if (length(missing_fits) > 0) message("no fit yet: ", paste(missing_fits, collapse = ", "))
jobs_fit = contrast_jobs %>% filter(job %in% names(model_files)[file.exists(model_files)])

# phylogenetic order for plots and tables: tips of the pruned tree from the unified analysis, in
# plotting order after ladderizing (so sister species are adjacent). species not in the tree go
# last, alphabetically.
phylo_tree = ape::ladderize(ape::read.tree(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "phylo_tree.nwk")))
is_tip = phylo_tree$edge[, 2] <= ape::Ntip(phylo_tree)
tip_order = phylo_tree$tip.label[phylo_tree$edge[is_tip, 2]]
fit_species = unique(jobs_fit$taxon_capture)
species_order = c(intersect(tip_order, fit_species), sort(setdiff(fit_species, tip_order)))

species_label = function(taxon) str_to_sentence(gsub("_", " ", taxon))
species_levels = species_label(species_order)

# level names as used in the model and as shown in tables / plots
level_labels = c(population = "site", pop_year = "site-year", pop_year_event = "event", all = "all levels")

# tier colors for all plots. tier = number of levels the contrast varies at (A 3 ... D 0);
# D = one mean contrast, no contrast sd
tier_colors = c(A = "#1B9E77", B = "#D95F02", C = "#7570B3", D = "#666666")

# the data each model saw, with grouping columns (to label group contrasts)
contrast_data = add_contrast_groups(brms_data) %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% fit_species)

```

# Process each fit
```{r}
# the fits are large (r. sierrae especially), so each is read, processed and dropped in turn:
# only summaries and a few numbers per draw are kept. the result is cached in intermediates/;
# set refresh = TRUE after replacing any fit (or when jobs change).
refresh = FALSE
results_file = file.path(intermediates_dir, "03_contrast_processed.rds")

# mean contrasts, contrast and intercept sds use all draws (16000 from round 3: 4 chains x 4000;
# cheap). group contrasts and intercepts (one per site, site-year, event) use 2000 evenly spaced
# draws, plenty for summaries; 1000 of those are kept for the stage 2 draw export and the
# per-draw season and year summaries.
ndraws_group = 2000
ndraws_export = 1000

# column-wise summary of a draws x groups matrix (contrasts or intercepts); columns named
# <prefix>_mean, <prefix>_median, ... and p_gt_0 for contrasts
summarise_cols = function(m, prefix = "contrast") {
  q = apply(m, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975))
  out = tibble(group_id = colnames(m),
               mean = colMeans(m),
               sd = apply(m, 2, sd),
               median = q[3, ],
               lower_50 = q[2, ],
               upper_50 = q[4, ],
               lower_95 = q[1, ],
               upper_95 = q[5, ])
  names(out)[-1] = paste0(prefix, "_", names(out)[-1])
  if (prefix == "contrast") out$p_gt_0 = colMeans(m > 0)
  out
}

process_contrast_fit = function(fit, job_row) {
  health = conv_check(fit) %>% mutate(job = job_row$job, .before = 1)

  # parts with a stage term: prefix of their parameter names, and the sign that turns the
  # coefficient into "subadult - adult, positive = subadults more infected"
  # has_pop_year / has_event: levels present in that part (R2)
  # the same sign is applied to the intercepts, so for prevalence they are -hu: higher = more
  # prevalent (prevalence = 1 - plogis(hu) = plogis(-hu)). flipping both signs leaves the
  # intercept-contrast correlation unchanged.
  parts = tibble(part = c("prevalence", "load"),
                 pre = c("hu_", ""),
                 sign = c(-1, 1),
                 tier = c(job_row$tier_hu, job_row$tier_mu),
                 has_pop_year = c(job_row$hu_has_pop_year, job_row$mu_has_pop_year),
                 has_event = c(job_row$hu_has_event, job_row$mu_has_event)) %>%
    filter(tier != "none")

  dr = as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^(b|sd|cor)_", regex = TRUE)
  n_draws = nrow(dr)
  ids_group = round(seq(1, n_draws, length.out = ndraws_group))
  ids_export = ids_group[round(seq(1, ndraws_group, length.out = ndraws_export))]
  rows_export = match(ids_export, ids_group)   # rows of a draws (ids_group) x units matrix

  # which population / site-year each event belongs to (ids are unique, so this is a lookup).
  # fit$data only keeps variables in the formula, so pop_year / pop_year_event are missing when
  # both parts drop those levels (R2); they're only needed when a part has those levels anyway
  units = fit$data %>%
    distinct(across(any_of(c("population", "pop_year", "pop_year_event")))) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.character))

  # group-level deviations of one term (coef: "stage_c", "hu_stage_c", "Intercept",
  # "hu_Intercept") for one grouping factor: draws (ids_group) x levels matrix. ranef() keeps the
  # data's level names (some contain parentheses / apostrophes)
  re_term = function(group, coef) {
    re = ranef(fit, summary = FALSE, groups = group)[[group]]
    m = re[ids_group, , coef]
    if (is.null(dim(m))) m = matrix(m, ncol = 1, dimnames = list(NULL, dimnames(re)[[2]]))
    m
  }

  # group values of one term down the hierarchy (unsigned):
  #   site       = b + r_population
  #   site-year  = site + r_pop_year
  #   event      = site-year + r_pop_year_event   (site + r_pop_year_event without a site-year
  #                                                level for this term)
  # `levels` = the levels where this term varies: for the contrast the tier's slope levels, for
  # the intercept every level present in the part
  build_group_mats = function(b, levels, coef) {
    m_pop = b[ids_group] + re_term("population", coef)   # b recycles down each column (one per draw)
    mats = list(population = m_pop)
    if ("pop_year" %in% levels) {
      r = re_term("pop_year", coef)
      mats$pop_year = m_pop[, units$population[match(colnames(r), units$pop_year)], drop = FALSE] + r
      colnames(mats$pop_year) = colnames(r)
    }
    if ("pop_year_event" %in% levels) {
      r = re_term("pop_year_event", coef)
      parent = if ("pop_year" %in% levels) {
        mats$pop_year[, units$pop_year[match(colnames(r), units$pop_year_event)], drop = FALSE]
      } else {
        m_pop[, units$population[match(colnames(r), units$pop_year_event)], drop = FALSE]
      }
      mats$pop_year_event = parent + r
      colnames(mats$pop_year_event) = colnames(r)
    }
    mats
  }

  per_part = pmap(parts, function(part, pre, sign, tier, has_pop_year, has_event) {
    b = dr[[paste0("b_", pre, "stage_c")]]
    intercept = dr[[paste0("b_", pre, "Intercept")]]

    # mean contrast, plus readable versions at a typical site / year / event (all random effects
    # at 0, the same reference as the contrast):
    #   linear predictor of each stage: adult = intercept - 0.5 b, subadult = intercept + 0.5 b
    #   prevalence part: prevalence of each stage (%) = 100 * (1 - plogis(hu)); typical_effect =
    #     the difference in percentage points
    #   load part: median load density among positives of each stage = exp(mu); typical_effect =
    #     the fold difference exp(b)
    # computed before tibble(): inside tibble(), `part` would refer to the column just created
    lin_adult = intercept - 0.5 * b
    lin_subadult = intercept + 0.5 * b
    if (part == "prevalence") {
      level_adult = 100 * (1 - plogis(lin_adult))
      level_subadult = 100 * (1 - plogis(lin_subadult))
      typical_effect = level_subadult - level_adult
    } else {
      level_adult = exp(lin_adult)
      level_subadult = exp(lin_subadult)
      typical_effect = exp(b)
    }
    species_draws = tibble(job = job_row$job, part = part, .draw = seq_len(n_draws),
                           contrast = sign * b, typical_effect = typical_effect,
                           level_adult = level_adult, level_subadult = level_subadult)

    # ---- intercepts (every tier, D included): overall infection at each level ----
    # intercept sds per level present (R2) and their variance shares; group intercepts (the
    # midpoint of the two stages; signed: -hu for prevalence, mu for load)
    int_levels = contrast_levels(has_pop_year, has_event)
    intercept_draws = map_dfr(int_levels, function(g) {
      tibble(job = job_row$job, part = part, level = g, .draw = seq_len(n_draws),
             sd_intercept = dr[[paste0("sd_", g, "__", pre, "Intercept")]])
    }) %>%
      group_by(.draw) %>%
      mutate(share_intercept = sd_intercept^2 / sum(sd_intercept^2)) %>%
      ungroup()
    int_mats = map(build_group_mats(intercept, int_levels, paste0(pre, "Intercept")), ~ sign * .x)
    intercept_summary = imap_dfr(int_mats, function(m, level) {
      summarise_cols(m, "intercept") %>% mutate(level = level, .before = 1)
    }) %>%
      mutate(job = job_row$job, part = part, .before = 1)
    int_unit_draws = map(int_mats, ~ .x[rows_export, , drop = FALSE])

    # mean-contrast draws for the stage 2 export (all tiers)
    export_mean = species_draws %>%
      filter(.draw %in% ids_export) %>%
      transmute(job, part, quantity = "mean_contrast", level = NA_character_,
                group_id = NA_character_, .draw, value = contrast)

    intercept_parts = list(intercept_draws = intercept_draws, intercept_summary = intercept_summary,
                           int_unit_draws = int_unit_draws)

    # tier D: one mean contrast, no contrast sds and no group contrasts
    groups = contrast_slope_groups(tier, has_pop_year, has_event)
    if (length(groups) == 0) {
      return(c(list(species_draws = species_draws, level_draws = NULL, group_summary = NULL,
                    export_draws = export_mean, unit_draws = NULL), intercept_parts))
    }

    # contrast sds, correlations and sign consistency per modeled level
    level_draws = map_dfr(groups, function(g) {
      tibble(job = job_row$job, part = part, level = g, .draw = seq_len(n_draws),
             sd = dr[[paste0("sd_", g, "__", pre, "stage_c")]],
             cor = dr[[paste0("cor_", g, "__", pre, "Intercept__", pre, "stage_c")]])
    }) %>%
      group_by(.draw) %>%
      mutate(share = sd^2 / sum(sd^2)) %>%
      ungroup()

    # "all levels": a new event in a new year at a new site, combining the modeled levels (levels
    # without a contrast slope in this tier count as 0)
    level_all = level_draws %>%
      group_by(job, part, .draw) %>%
      summarise(sd = sqrt(sum(sd^2)), .groups = "drop") %>%
      mutate(level = "all", cor = NA_real_, share = NA_real_)

    level_draws = bind_rows(level_draws, level_all) %>%
      left_join(species_draws %>% select(.draw, contrast), by = ".draw") %>%
      mutate(sign_consistency = pnorm(abs(contrast) / sd)) %>%
      select(-contrast)

    # group contrasts (site, and site-year / event where the tier has those slopes), signed
    group_mats = map(build_group_mats(b, groups, paste0(pre, "stage_c")), ~ sign * .x)

    group_summary = imap_dfr(group_mats, function(m, level) {
      summarise_cols(m) %>% mutate(level = level, .before = 1)
    }) %>%
      mutate(job = job_row$job, part = part, .before = 1)

    # site-year and event contrast draws (signed, 1000 draws x units, as matrices to stay small),
    # for the per-draw season and year summaries ("Patterns across the season and years")
    unit_draws = map(group_mats[intersect(c("pop_year", "pop_year_event"), names(group_mats))],
                     ~ .x[rows_export, , drop = FALSE])

    # stage 2 draw export: mean contrast, contrast sds and population contrasts, 1000 draws
    export_draws = bind_rows(
      export_mean,
      level_draws %>%
        filter(.draw %in% ids_export, level != "all") %>%
        transmute(job, part, quantity = "contrast_sd", level, group_id = NA_character_,
                  .draw, value = sd),
      as_tibble(group_mats$population[rows_export, , drop = FALSE]) %>%
        mutate(.draw = ids_export) %>%
        pivot_longer(-.draw, names_to = "group_id", values_to = "value") %>%
        transmute(job = job_row$job, part = part, quantity = "group_contrast",
                  level = "population", group_id, .draw, value))

    c(list(species_draws = species_draws, level_draws = level_draws, group_summary = group_summary,
           export_draws = export_draws, unit_draws = unit_draws), intercept_parts)
  })
  names(per_part) = parts$part

  list(health = health,
       species_draws = map_dfr(per_part, "species_draws"),
       level_draws = map_dfr(per_part, "level_draws"),
       group_summary = map_dfr(per_part, "group_summary"),
       export_draws = map_dfr(per_part, "export_draws"),
       # unit_draws[[part]][[level]]: draws x units matrix of contrasts (NULL for tier D parts)
       unit_draws = map(per_part, "unit_draws"),
       intercept_draws = map_dfr(per_part, "intercept_draws"),
       intercept_summary = map_dfr(per_part, "intercept_summary"),
       # int_unit_draws[[part]][[level]]: draws x units matrix of intercepts (every part)
       int_unit_draws = map(per_part, "int_unit_draws"))
}

if (!refresh && file.exists(results_file)) {
  processed = readRDS(results_file)
  if (!setequal(names(processed), jobs_fit$job)) {
    message("cached jobs differ from the fits available: set refresh = TRUE to reprocess")
  }
  if (!all(map_lgl(processed, ~ all(c("unit_draws", "int_unit_draws") %in% names(.x))))) {
    message("cache made before site-year / event and intercept draws were kept: set refresh = TRUE ",
            "for the season / year summaries and the intercept sections")
  }
} else {
  processed = map(seq_len(nrow(jobs_fit)), function(k) {
    job_row = jobs_fit[k, ]
    message("processing ", job_row$job)
    fit = readRDS(model_files[[job_row$job]])
    out = process_contrast_fit(fit, job_row)
    rm(fit)
    gc()
    out
  })
  names(processed) = jobs_fit$job
  saveRDS(processed, results_file)
}

# stack each component across jobs
stack_component = function(name) map_dfr(processed, name)
fit_convergence = stack_component("health")
species_draws = stack_component("species_draws")
level_draws = stack_component("level_draws")
group_summary = stack_component("group_summary")
export_draws = stack_component("export_draws")
# intercepts (overall infection). an old cache has none: empty tables with the right columns
# (and NA stage levels), so the intercept sections come out empty instead of failing
intercept_draws = stack_component("intercept_draws")
intercept_summary = stack_component("intercept_summary")
if (nrow(intercept_draws) == 0) {
  intercept_draws = tibble(job = character(), part = character(), level = character(),
                           .draw = integer(), sd_intercept = double(), share_intercept = double())
  intercept_summary = tibble(job = character(), part = character(), level = character(),
                             group_id = character(), intercept_median = double(),
                             intercept_lower_95 = double(), intercept_upper_95 = double())
}
for (v in c("level_adult", "level_subadult")) {
  if (!v %in% names(species_draws)) species_draws[[v]] = NA_real_
}

```

# Fit health
```{r}
# a compact flag carried with every result, so a problem fit is not read uncritically. the full
# checks (LOO, predictive checks, prior sensitivity) are in 02_contrast_modeling.qmd.
# thresholds as in conv_check (season_check_functions.R); a few divergences are tolerated.
fit_health = fit_convergence %>%
  mutate(fit_ok = max_rhat < 1.01 & min_ess_bulk > 400 & min_ess_tail > 400 &
           n_divergent <= 5 & min_ebfmi > 0.3) %>%
  left_join(jobs_fit %>% select(job, taxon_capture, variant, tier_hu, tier_mu), by = "job")

(fit_health_check = fit_health %>%
  select(job, tier_hu, tier_mu, n_obs, max_rhat, worst_rhat_par, min_ess_bulk, min_ess_tail,
         n_divergent, min_ebfmi, fit_ok) %>%
  arrange(fit_ok, desc(n_divergent)))

```

# Summaries
```{r}
# job-level attributes carried with every summary
job_info = jobs_fit %>%
  select(job, taxon_capture, variant, tier_hu, tier_mu, d_reason_hu, d_reason_mu, n_adult,
         n_subadult, flag_time_segregated) %>%
  left_join(fit_health %>% select(job, fit_ok), by = "job") %>%
  mutate(job_label = if_else(variant == "main", species_label(taxon_capture),
                             paste0(species_label(taxon_capture), " (", variant, ")")))

# ---- mean contrast (Q1) ----
contrast_agg = f_draw_agg(species_draws, c("job", "part"), "contrast")

# readable versions at a typical site, year and event (random effects at 0): the difference
# (percentage points or fold) and each stage's level (prevalence %, or median load density among
# positives). levels are within-species context only: labs differ, so never compare them across
# species. (item 1)
q_med = function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
q_lo = function(x) quantile(x, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
q_hi = function(x) quantile(x, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
typical_agg = species_draws %>%
  group_by(job, part) %>%
  summarise(across(c(typical_effect, level_adult, level_subadult),
                   list(median = q_med, lower_95 = q_lo, upper_95 = q_hi), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(typical_effect_unit = if_else(part == "prevalence", "percentage points", "fold"),
         level_unit = if_else(part == "prevalence", "% prevalence", "median load among positives"))

# ---- contrast sds, contraction, sign consistency, shares, correlations (Q2-Q5) ----
# exponential(2) prior on each contrast sd: variance 1 / rate^2 = 0.25
prior_sd_var = 1 / 2^2
# a level counts as "informed" when the data at least halve the prior variance of its sd.
# a reading aid for tables and fading in plots, not a test.
informed_contraction = 0.5

# ---- intercepts: how much overall infection varies at each level (items 3, 5) ----
# intercept sd and variance share per level present, every part (tier D included)
intercept_level_summary = intercept_draws %>%
  group_by(job, part, level) %>%
  summarise(sd_intercept_median = median(sd_intercept),
            sd_intercept_lower_95 = quantile(sd_intercept, 0.025),
            sd_intercept_upper_95 = quantile(sd_intercept, 0.975),
            share_intercept_median = median(share_intercept),
            .groups = "drop")

# ratio of contrast sd to intercept sd at each level with a contrast slope, per draw: < 1 = the
# subadult - adult gap varies less than overall infection does at that level. intercept shares
# recomputed over the same (slope) levels as the contrast shares, so the two profiles compare
# like with like
sd_ratio_draws = level_draws %>%
  filter(level != "all") %>%
  inner_join(intercept_draws %>% select(job, part, level, .draw, sd_intercept),
             by = c("job", "part", "level", ".draw")) %>%
  group_by(job, part, .draw) %>%
  mutate(sd_ratio = sd / sd_intercept,
         share_intercept_same_levels = sd_intercept^2 / sum(sd_intercept^2)) %>%
  ungroup()

sd_ratio_summary = sd_ratio_draws %>%
  group_by(job, part, level) %>%
  summarise(sd_ratio_median = median(sd_ratio),
            sd_ratio_lower_95 = quantile(sd_ratio, 0.025),
            sd_ratio_upper_95 = quantile(sd_ratio, 0.975),
            share_intercept_same_levels_median = median(share_intercept_same_levels),
            .groups = "drop")

level_summary = level_draws %>%
  group_by(job, part, level) %>%
  summarise(sd_median = median(sd),
            sd_lower_95 = quantile(sd, 0.025),
            sd_upper_95 = quantile(sd, 0.975),
            contraction = if_else(first(level) == "all", NA_real_, 1 - var(sd) / prior_sd_var),
            sign_consistency_median = median(sign_consistency),
            sign_consistency_lower_95 = quantile(sign_consistency, 0.025),
            sign_consistency_upper_95 = quantile(sign_consistency, 0.975),
            share_median = median(share),
            cor_median = median(cor),
            cor_lower_95 = quantile(cor, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
            cor_upper_95 = quantile(cor, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  # intercept sd, sd ratio and same-level intercept share next to each contrast sd (empty
  # columns for an old cache)
  left_join(intercept_level_summary %>% select(job, part, level, starts_with("sd_intercept")),
            by = c("job", "part", "level")) %>%
  left_join(sd_ratio_summary, by = c("job", "part", "level")) %>%
  mutate(informed = contraction >= informed_contraction,
         level = factor(level, levels = names(level_labels)))

# ---- one row per job x part ----
species_summary = job_info %>%
  inner_join(contrast_agg, by = "job") %>%
  left_join(typical_agg, by = c("job", "part")) %>%
  # per part: tier, why it is D (if so), and one caveat label for plots and tables. a
  # between-population part is always D; time-segregated is the one caveat flag (any tier,
  # including D for few co-sampled sites; flag_time_segregated comes from 01's job table)
  mutate(tier = if_else(part == "prevalence", tier_hu, tier_mu),
         d_reason = if_else(part == "prevalence", d_reason_hu, d_reason_mu),
         flag = case_when(d_reason == "between-population" ~ "between-population",
                          flag_time_segregated ~ "time-segregated",
                          .default = "none")) %>%
  left_join(level_summary %>%
              select(job, part, level, sd_median, sd_lower_95, sd_upper_95, contraction,
                     sign_consistency_median, share_median, cor_median) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = level,
                          values_from = c(sd_median, sd_lower_95, sd_upper_95, contraction,
                                          sign_consistency_median, share_median, cor_median),
                          names_glue = "{level}_{.value}"),
            by = c("job", "part")) %>%
  # "all levels" has no share, correlation or contraction of its own. dropped by name: dropping
  # every all-NA column would also drop d_reason when no job is tier D
  select(-any_of(c("all_contraction", "all_share_median", "all_cor_median")))

```

```{r}
# readable table: mean contrast, typical-site effect and support
fmt_ci = function(m, l, u, digits = 2) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f [%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"), m, l, u)
}

# stage levels: prevalence in %, loads with 2 significant digits (they span orders of magnitude)
fmt_level = function(part, m, l, u) {
  if_else(part == "prevalence", sprintf("%.0f%% [%.0f, %.0f]", m, l, u),
          paste0(signif(m, 2), " [", signif(l, 2), ", ", signif(u, 2), "]"))
}

plot_main %>%
  arrange(part, species) %>%
  transmute(species, part, tier, flag, fit_ok,
            contrast = fmt_ci(contrast_median, contrast_lower_95, contrast_upper_95),
            typical_effect = paste(fmt_ci(typical_effect_median, typical_effect_lower_95,
                                          typical_effect_upper_95, 1), typical_effect_unit),
            # each stage at a typical site / year / event: what the contrast is a difference of
            # (within-species context; levels are not comparable across species)
            adult = fmt_level(part, level_adult_median, level_adult_lower_95, level_adult_upper_95),
            subadult = fmt_level(part, level_subadult_median, level_subadult_lower_95,
                                 level_subadult_upper_95),
            level_unit,
            pd = round(contrast_pd, 3), support = contrast_support)
```

## Prevalence vs load contrasts: net and median effect
```{r}
#| fig-height: 8

# versions of the net effect and median effect scatters in
# size_bd_unified/03_size_bd_unified_analysis.qmd, built from the main contrast fits, one point
# per species. both parts are already signed "positive = subadults higher" here (the unified
# script flips the hu contrast by hand with -hu_...), so no sign change is needed.
#   net effect = 2 * P(contrast > 0) - 1 (from f_draw_agg): -1 = certainly lower in subadults,
#                +1 = certainly higher, 0 = no idea. a certainty scale, not an effect size.
#   median     = posterior median contrast (logit prevalence on x, log load among positives on y)

# convergence flag, as elsewhere.
effect_wide = species_summary %>%
  filter(variant == "main") %>%

  pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = c(contrast_median, contrast_net_effect)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(contrast_median_prevalence), !is.na(contrast_median_load)) %>%
  mutate(species = species_label(taxon_capture))
```

# Consistency profile (Q2-Q5)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 10

# one tile per species x level. two separate encodings:
#   fill and number = sign consistency (probability a new site / site-year / event keeps the
#     sign of the mean contrast)
#   dashed outline + grey italic number = the contrast sd at that level is mostly prior
#     (contraction < informed_contraction), so the consistency mostly reflects the prior: a large
#     mean with a prior-sized sd reads as consistent whatever the data say
# (the fill used to be faded for uninformed levels, which made an uninformed 98% look like an
# informed 70%; the outline keeps the colour for consistency only.)
# "all levels" combines the modeled levels; it is marked uninformed when none of them is informed.
# blank = level not modeled in this species' tier; "D" = no contrast sd at any level.
# built from every main job x part (so tier D parts, which have no levels, still get a row)
any_informed = level_summary %>%
  filter(level != "all") %>%
  group_by(job, part) %>%
  summarise(any_informed = any(informed), .groups = "drop")

plot_profile = species_summary %>%
  filter(variant == "main") %>%
  select(job, taxon_capture, part, tier) %>%
  crossing(level = factor(names(level_labels), levels = names(level_labels))) %>%
  left_join(level_summary %>% select(job, part, level, sign_consistency_median, informed),
            by = c("job", "part", "level")) %>%
  left_join(any_informed, by = c("job", "part")) %>%
  mutate(informed = if_else(level == "all", any_informed, informed),
         uninformed = !is.na(sign_consistency_median) & !informed,
         species = factor(species_label(taxon_capture), levels = rev(species_levels)),
         part = factor(part, levels = c("prevalence", "load")),
         level = factor(level_labels[as.character(level)], levels = level_labels),
         label = case_when(tier == "D" & level == "site" ~ "D",
                           is.na(sign_consistency_median) ~ "",
                           .default = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * sign_consistency_median)),
         # number and outline colour follow the fill so both stay readable: white on dark tiles
         ink = if_else(coalesce(sign_consistency_median >= 0.85, FALSE), "white", "black"),
         face = if_else(uninformed, "italic", "plain"))

p_profile = ggplot(plot_profile, aes(x = level, y = species)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = sign_consistency_median), color = "white") +
  geom_tile(data = filter(plot_profile, uninformed), aes(color = ink), fill = NA,
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, width = 0.86, height = 0.78) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label, color = ink, fontface = face), size = 2.6) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7F7F7", high = "#2166AC", limits = c(0.5, 1), na.value = "grey97",
                      name = "sign\nconsistency") +
  facet_wrap(~ part) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       subtitle = paste0("% of new units keeping the sign of the mean contrast\n",
                         "dashed outline + italic = contrast sd mostly prior (contraction < ",
                         informed_contraction, "): the consistency then mostly reflects the prior")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), panel.grid = element_blank())

p_profile

            share = round(share_median, 2), informed) %>%
```

# Does the gap change with overall infection? (Q6)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 11

# the model estimates, at each level with a contrast slope, the correlation between a unit's
# intercept (overall infection: the midpoint of the two stages) and its contrast
# (cor_<level>__Intercept__stage_c). positive = sites / site-years / events with more Bd overall
# have a larger subadult - adult gap (e.g. subadults hit harder in outbreaks); negative = the
# gap shrinks when infection is high (e.g. everyone infected). for prevalence both are on the
# prevalence scale (-hu), for load on log load among positives.
# correlations are unitless, so they can be compared across species. the correlation's prior is
# lkj(2) (mildly toward 0); where the contrast sd is mostly prior, the correlation is weakly
# informed too and reads as prior. read the parameter, not the scatter below: shrinkage pulls
# group medians toward the mean, which distorts their apparent correlation.
plot_cor = level_summary %>%
  filter(level != "all") %>%
  inner_join(job_info %>% filter(variant == "main"), by = "job") %>%
  mutate(species = factor(species_label(taxon_capture), levels = rev(species_levels)),
         part = factor(part, levels = c("prevalence", "load")),
         level = factor(level_labels[as.character(level)], levels = level_labels),
         informed = if_else(informed, "contrast sd informed", "contrast sd mostly prior"))

p_cor = ggplot(plot_cor, aes(x = cor_median, y = species, color = level, shape = informed)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = cor_lower_95, xmax = cor_upper_95), size = 0.3,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), fill = "white") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`contrast sd informed` = 16, `contrast sd mostly prior` = 21), name = NULL) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "level") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~ part) +
  labs(x = "correlation of intercept (overall infection) and contrast (median, 95%)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "positive = more Bd overall goes with a larger subadult - adult gap") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), legend.position = "bottom")

p_cor

# the same as a table, informed levels only
(intercept_contrast_correlations = level_summary %>%
  filter(level != "all", informed) %>%
  inner_join(job_info %>% select(job, job_label), by = "job") %>%
  transmute(job_label, part, level = level_labels[as.character(level)],
            cor = fmt_ci(cor_median, cor_lower_95, cor_upper_95)) %>%
  arrange(part, level, job_label))
```

# Contrast variation against overall infection variation (items 3, 5)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 11

# ratio of contrast sd to intercept sd at each level (per draw): < 1 = the subadult - adult gap
# varies less than overall infection at that level ("Bd swings a lot between events, the age gap
# barely moves"); > 1 = the gap is the less stable of the two. intercept sds are informed by
# every unit, contrast sds mainly by co-sampled ones; where the contrast sd is mostly prior the
# ratio mostly reflects that prior. load ratios can be compared across species (lab offsets shift
# log loads without changing their spread); prevalence ratios are read within species.
plot_ratio = level_summary %>%
  filter(level != "all", !is.na(sd_ratio_median)) %>%
  inner_join(job_info %>% filter(variant == "main"), by = "job") %>%
  mutate(species = factor(species_label(taxon_capture), levels = rev(species_levels)),
         part = factor(part, levels = c("prevalence", "load")),
         level = factor(level_labels[as.character(level)], levels = level_labels),
         informed = if_else(informed, "contrast sd informed", "contrast sd mostly prior"))

p_sd_ratio = if (nrow(plot_ratio) > 0) {
  ggplot(plot_ratio, aes(x = sd_ratio_median, y = species, color = level, shape = informed)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, color = "grey60") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = sd_ratio_lower_95, xmax = sd_ratio_upper_95), size = 0.3,
                    position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), fill = "white") +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`contrast sd informed` = 16, `contrast sd mostly prior` = 21), name = NULL) +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "level") +
    facet_wrap(~ part) +
    labs(x = "contrast sd / intercept sd (median, 95%; log scale)", y = NULL,
         subtitle = "< 1 = the subadult - adult gap varies less than overall infection at that level") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), legend.position = "bottom")
} else NULL
p_sd_ratio

# where does overall infection vary, and where does the gap vary? variance shares of the
# intercept and of the contrast over the same levels (species whose contrast varies at >= 2
# levels: tiers A and B). contrast shares at prior-dominated levels are mostly the prior (about
# equal shares by construction), marked with lighter bars.
plot_shares = level_summary %>%
  filter(level != "all", !is.na(share_intercept_same_levels_median)) %>%
  inner_join(job_info %>% filter(variant == "main"), by = "job") %>%
  group_by(job, part) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(taxon_capture, part, level, informed,
            contrast = share_median, intercept = share_intercept_same_levels_median) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(contrast, intercept), names_to = "term", values_to = "share") %>%
  mutate(species = factor(species_label(taxon_capture), levels = rev(species_levels)),
         part = factor(part, levels = c("prevalence", "load")),
         level = factor(level_labels[as.character(level)], levels = level_labels),
         term = factor(term, levels = c("intercept", "contrast"),
                       labels = c("overall infection (intercept)", "subadult - adult gap (contrast)")),
         bar_alpha = if_else(term == "subadult - adult gap (contrast)" & !informed, "mostly prior", "informed"))

p_share_compare = if (nrow(plot_shares) > 0) {
  ggplot(plot_shares, aes(x = share, y = species, fill = level, alpha = bar_alpha)) +
    geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "level") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(informed = 1, `mostly prior` = 0.4), name = "contrast sd") +
    facet_grid(part ~ term) +
    labs(x = "variance share (median)", y = NULL,
         subtitle = paste0("same levels in both panels; shares of the contrast at prior-dominated levels are mostly the prior\n",
                           "bars stack the median share of each level, so they need not sum to exactly 1")) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic", size = 7), legend.position = "bottom")
} else NULL
p_share_compare

# intercept variance shares over every level present, all species (supplement): where overall
# infection varies most, including tier C and D species
(intercept_share_table = intercept_level_summary %>%
  inner_join(job_info %>% filter(variant == "main") %>% select(job, taxon_capture), by = "job") %>%
  transmute(species = factor(species_label(taxon_capture), levels = species_levels), part,
            level = level_labels[level],
            sd = fmt_ci(sd_intercept_median, sd_intercept_lower_95, sd_intercept_upper_95),
            share = round(share_intercept_median, 2)) %>%
  arrange(part, species, factor(level, levels = level_labels)))
```

```{r}
interpretation = species_summary %>%

              filter(level != "all") %>%

              summarise(informed_levels = paste(level_labels[as.character(level[informed])], collapse = ", "),

                                  NA_character_))

interpretation

```

# Group contrasts
```{r}
# labels for each group: swabs and positives per stage, co-sampled flags (for prevalence: co;
# for load: co_load), and for events their survey dates (first, last, median)
unit_flags = imap_dfr(c(population = "population", pop_year = "pop_year", pop_year_event = "pop_year_event"),
                      function(unit, level) co_unit_flags(contrast_data, unit) %>% mutate(level = level))

event_info = contrast_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, pop_year_event) %>%
  summarise(population = first(population), year = first(year),
            event_start = min(date), event_end = max(date), median_date = median(date),
            n_dates = n_distinct(date), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # timing within the season: day of year of the median swab date (events are survey runs of
  # up to 14 days, so this places them to within a week)
  mutate(event_span = as.numeric(event_end - event_start) + 1,
         event_doy = yday(median_date))

popyear_info = contrast_data %>%
  distinct(taxon_capture, pop_year, population, year)

# adds to a per-unit table (job, part, level, group_id, ...) the species, swab and positive
# counts per stage, the co-sampled flag of that part, population, year and event dates
label_units = function(d) {
  d %>%
    left_join(jobs_fit %>% select(job, taxon_capture, variant), by = "job") %>%
    left_join(unit_flags, by = c("taxon_capture", "level", "group_id" = "unit_id")) %>%
    mutate(co_sampled = if_else(part == "prevalence", co, co_load)) %>%
    left_join(popyear_info %>% rename(py_population = population, py_year = year),
              by = c("taxon_capture", "group_id" = "pop_year")) %>%
    left_join(event_info %>% rename(ev_population = population, ev_year = year),
              by = c("taxon_capture", "group_id" = "pop_year_event")) %>%
    mutate(population = case_when(level == "population" ~ group_id,
                                  level == "pop_year" ~ py_population,
                                  level == "pop_year_event" ~ ev_population),
           year = coalesce(py_year, ev_year))
}
unit_label_cols = c("job", "taxon_capture", "variant", "part", "level", "group_id", "population",
                    "year", "event_start", "event_end", "event_span", "n_dates", "median_date",
                    "event_doy", "n_adult", "n_subadult", "n_pos_adult", "n_pos_subadult", "co_sampled")

# group intercepts: overall infection of every site, site-year and event (midpoint of the two
# stages; prevalence on the -hu logit scale, load on log load among positives), all parts and
# tiers. for the intercept-contrast scatter and the absolute patterns
group_intercepts = intercept_summary %>%
  label_units() %>%
  select(all_of(unit_label_cols), starts_with("intercept_"))

# group contrasts, with the unit's intercept alongside
group_contrasts = group_summary %>%
  label_units() %>%
  left_join(intercept_summary %>% select(job, part, level, group_id, intercept_median,
                                         intercept_lower_95, intercept_upper_95),
            by = c("job", "part", "level", "group_id")) %>%
  select(all_of(unit_label_cols), starts_with("contrast_"), p_gt_0, starts_with("intercept_"))

# how many group contrasts rest on co-sampled units
group_contrasts %>%
  count(part, level, co_sampled)
```

## Population contrasts
```{r}
#| fig-height: 14
#| fig-width: 14

# one panel per species (main fits): each site's contrast, co-sampled sites solid. dashed line =
# the species mean contrast. non-co-sampled sites sit near the mean by construction (shrinkage).
plot_population_contrasts = function(part_name) {
  d = group_contrasts %>%
    filter(variant == "main", part == part_name, level == "population") %>%
    mutate(species = factor(species_label(taxon_capture), levels = species_levels),
           # sites ordered by median contrast within each species (lowest at the bottom). the key
           # is species + site: some site names occur in several species (e.g. shared sierra or
           # vermont ponds), and a factor holds each name once, so ordering on the site name alone
           # would fix a shared site at its position in the first species. labels are hidden
           site_key = fct_reorder(paste(species, population, sep = "__"), contrast_median))
  means = plot_main %>%
    filter(part == part_name) %>%
    transmute(species = factor(as.character(species), levels = species_levels), contrast_median)

  ggplot(d, aes(x = contrast_median, y = site_key, alpha = co_sampled)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
    geom_vline(data = means, aes(xintercept = contrast_median), linetype = "dashed", color = "#2166AC") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = contrast_lower_95, xmax = contrast_upper_95), size = 0.15) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.3), name = "co-sampled") +
    facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free", ncol = 6) +
    labs(x = paste0(part_name, " contrast (median, 95% interval)"), y = NULL) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "italic", size = 7), legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

## Intercept against contrast by unit (Q6 illustration)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-width: 14

# each co-sampled unit's contrast against its intercept (medians), one panel per species and
# level with an estimated correlation. an illustration of p_cor only: shrinkage pulls both
# medians toward their parents, so the cloud's apparent slope is not the estimate; the panel
# label gives the model's correlation (median, 95%). species x levels with an informed contrast
# sd only, where the correlation can carry information
plot_int_contrast = function(part_name) {
  keep = level_summary %>%
    filter(level != "all", informed, part == part_name) %>%
    transmute(job, level = as.character(level),
              cor_label = paste0("r = ", fmt_ci(cor_median, cor_lower_95, cor_upper_95)))
  d = group_contrasts %>%
    filter(variant == "main", part == part_name, co_sampled) %>%
    inner_join(keep, by = c("job", "level")) %>%
    mutate(panel = paste0(species_label(taxon_capture), ", ", level_labels[level], "\n", cor_label))
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)
  d = d %>%
    mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel[order(match(taxon_capture, species_order),
                                                             match(level, names(level_labels)))])))
  ggplot(d, aes(x = intercept_median, y = contrast_median)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
    geom_point(size = 0.9, alpha = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free", ncol = 5) +
    labs(x = paste0("unit intercept (overall infection; ", if (part_name == "prevalence") "logit prevalence" else "log load among positives", ")"),
         y = paste0(part_name, " contrast"),
         subtitle = paste0(part_name, ": co-sampled units (medians); panel label = estimated intercept-contrast correlation")) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
}
```

```{r}
# does the contrast drift or swing between years? co-sampled site-years only, one panel per

  if (length(species_ab) == 0) return(NULL)   # no tier A / B species for this part

         subtitle = "co-sampled site-years (median, 95%), lines join a site's years; grey band = species mean (95%)") +
```

## Patterns across the season and years (per draw)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 14

# single event and site-year contrasts are imprecise (few swabs each), so their intervals mostly
# include 0. patterns are read instead from summaries ACROSS many units, computed within each
# posterior draw and then summarized over draws: averaging over units cancels much of the noise,
# and working draw by draw keeps the uncertainty honest (units in one draw share the species,
# site and site-year terms, which separate medians and intervals hide).
#
# caveats:
#   - the model has no seasonal or year term: units are exchangeable, so partial pooling pulls
#     any trend toward 0. a pattern that shows despite that is convincing; its absence is not
#     proof there is none. the formal test is stage 2 (unit contrasts against time / climate).
#   - pooled comparisons (across site-years or sites) mix the trend with which units were
#     sampled when. the within-unit slopes avoid this, using only differences inside a
#     site-year (season) or a site (years).
#   - where the event (site-year) contrast sd is mostly prior, units sit near their parent by
#     construction and no pattern can show: the "informed" column says which levels to read.
#   - exploratory: no thresholds, read the size and sign agreement (pd) of the summaries.
#
# the same helpers serve the contrasts here and the intercepts (absolute patterns) below.
# needs the unit draws kept in processing (refresh = TRUE once after they were added)
unit_draws = function(job, part, level) processed[[job]]$unit_draws[[part]][[level]]
int_unit_draws = function(job, part, level) processed[[job]]$int_unit_draws[[part]][[level]]
if (!any(map_lgl(processed, ~ length(.x$unit_draws) > 0))) {
  message("no site-year / event draws in the processed results (cache made before they were ",
          "kept): set refresh = TRUE in 'Process each fit'. season and year summaries skipped")
}

# summary table of per-draw columns (long, f_draw_agg). empty when no species produced draws
# (group_modify then returns no summary columns), so the section skips instead of failing
summarise_unit_draws = function(draws, cols) {
  if (!all(cols %in% names(draws)) || nrow(draws) == 0) return(tibble())
  draws %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(cols), names_to = "summary") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
    f_draw_agg(c("job", "taxon_capture", "part", "summary"), "value")
}

# per-draw least-squares slope of the units (columns of m) on x. with x centered within groups
# (site-years, sites), this is the pooled within-group slope: sum(m * x) / sum(x^2) needs no
# centering of m, because x sums to 0 within each group
draw_slope = function(m, x) as.vector(m %*% x) / sum(x^2)
center_within = function(x, g) x - ave(x, g)

informed_of = function(level_name) {
  level_summary %>%
    filter(level == level_name) %>%
    select(job, part, informed)
}

# events with their position in the species' season (season_day, on each species' seasonal
# calendar as in the event plot) and site-year
add_season_day = function(d) {
  d %>%
    left_join(season_origins, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
    mutate(origin_doy = coalesce(origin_doy, 1),
           season_day = (event_doy - origin_doy) %% 365,
           pop_year = paste(population, year, sep = "_"))
}

# per draw, from events (units: job, taxon_capture, part, group_id, season_day, pop_year) and a
# matrix getter get_m(job, part) (draws x events):
#   slope_within      change per 30 days, within site-years (site-years with >= 2 events)
#   slope_pooled      the same across all events (mixes in between-site-year timing)
#   late_minus_early  mean of the last third of the season minus the first third (thirds of the
#                     species' events by season_day; pooled)
season_pattern_draws = function(units, get_m) {
  units %>%
    group_by(job, taxon_capture, part) %>%
    group_modify(function(u, key) {
      m = get_m(key$job, key$part)
      if (is.null(m) || nrow(u) < 3) return(tibble())
      m = m[, u$group_id, drop = FALSE]
      multi = u$pop_year %in% names(which(table(u$pop_year) >= 2))
      x_within = center_within(u$season_day[multi], u$pop_year[multi])
      third = cut(rank(u$season_day, ties.method = "first"), 3, labels = c("early", "mid", "late"))
      tibble(.draw = seq_len(nrow(m)),
             slope_within = if (sum(multi) >= 2 && sum(x_within^2) > 0) {
               30 * draw_slope(m[, multi, drop = FALSE], x_within)
             } else NA_real_,
             slope_pooled = 30 * draw_slope(m, u$season_day - mean(u$season_day)),
             late_minus_early = rowMeans(m[, third == "late", drop = FALSE]) -
               rowMeans(m[, third == "early", drop = FALSE]))
    }) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# per draw, from site-years (units: job, taxon_capture, part, group_id, year, population):
#   slope_within  change per year within sites (sites with >= 2 site-years): a drift
#   slope_pooled  the same across all site-years (mixes in which sites were sampled when)
year_pattern_draws = function(units, get_m) {
  units %>%
    group_by(job, taxon_capture, part) %>%
    group_modify(function(u, key) {
      m = get_m(key$job, key$part)
      if (is.null(m) || nrow(u) < 3) return(tibble())
      m = m[, u$group_id, drop = FALSE]
      multi = u$population %in% names(which(table(u$population) >= 2))
      x_within = center_within(u$year[multi], u$population[multi])
      tibble(.draw = seq_len(nrow(m)),
             slope_within = if (sum(multi) >= 2 && sum(x_within^2) > 0) {
               draw_slope(m[, multi, drop = FALSE], x_within)
             } else NA_real_,
             slope_pooled = if (var(u$year) > 0) draw_slope(m, u$year - mean(u$year)) else NA_real_)
    }) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# per-draw seasonal curves: for 100 draws, a smooth (natural spline, 3 df) through that draw's
# event values against season_day. the spread of the curves is the uncertainty in the seasonal
# pattern; a band of curves that rises or falls together is a pattern even when each event's
# interval includes 0. pooled across site-years (see caveats). drawn only within 15 days of an
# observed event and broken across sampling gaps (a spline across a gap invents a shape), and
# only for species with >= 10 events. `transform` maps the fitted curve to the plotting scale
season_curve_draws = function(units, get_m, transform = identity) {
  units %>%
    group_by(job, taxon_capture, part) %>%
    group_modify(function(u, key) {
      m = get_m(key$job, key$part)
      if (is.null(m) || nrow(u) < 10) return(tibble())
      m = m[seq_len(min(100, nrow(m))), u$group_id, drop = FALSE]
      basis = splines::ns(u$season_day, df = 3)
      grid = seq(min(u$season_day), max(u$season_day), by = 1)
      near = vapply(grid, function(g) min(abs(g - u$season_day)) <= 15, logical(1))
      grid = grid[near]
      segment = cumsum(c(1, diff(grid) > 1))   # a new segment after each gap
      b = cbind(1, basis)
      coef = solve(crossprod(b), t(b) %*% t(m))   # (1 + 3) x draws
      fit = cbind(1, predict(basis, grid)) %*% coef
      tibble(season_day = rep(grid, ncol(fit)), segment = rep(segment, ncol(fit)),
             .draw = rep(seq_len(ncol(fit)), each = length(grid)), value = transform(as.vector(fit)))
    }) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# plot of per-draw curves over unit medians (pts: job, taxon_capture, season_day, point_value);
# facet_note: optional per-job suffix for the facet label (e.g. "event sd mostly prior")
plot_curves = function(curves, pts, part_name, y_label, subtitle, facet_note = NULL,
                       y_scale = NULL, zero_line = TRUE) {
  if (!"part" %in% names(curves)) return(NULL)   # no draws
  cu = curves %>% filter(part == part_name)
  if (nrow(cu) == 0) return(NULL)
  pts = pts %>% filter(part == part_name, job %in% cu$job)
  facet_labels = cu %>%
    distinct(job, taxon_capture) %>%
    left_join(if (is.null(facet_note)) tibble(job = character(), note = character()) else facet_note,
              by = "job") %>%
    arrange(match(taxon_capture, species_order)) %>%
    mutate(species = paste0(species_label(taxon_capture), coalesce(note, "")),
           species = factor(species, levels = species)) %>%
    select(job, species)
  p = ggplot(left_join(cu, facet_labels, by = "job"), aes(x = season_day, y = value)) +
    (if (zero_line) geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey60") else NULL) +
    geom_line(aes(group = interaction(.draw, segment)), alpha = 0.08, color = "#2166AC") +
    geom_point(data = left_join(pts, facet_labels, by = "job"), aes(y = point_value),
               size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
    labs(x = "day of the species' season (from its seasonal origin)", y = y_label, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic", size = 8))
  if (!is.null(y_scale)) p = p + y_scale
  p
}

# ---- the contrast through the season (tier A, co-sampled events) ----
season_units = group_contrasts %>%
  filter(variant == "main", level == "pop_year_event", co_sampled) %>%
  add_season_day()
get_event_contrasts = function(job, part) unit_draws(job, part, "pop_year_event")

season_draws = season_pattern_draws(season_units, get_event_contrasts)
season_summary = summarise_unit_draws(season_draws, c("slope_within", "slope_pooled", "late_minus_early"))
if (nrow(season_summary) > 0) season_summary = season_summary %>%
  left_join(season_units %>%
              group_by(job, part) %>%
              summarise(n_events = n(),
                        n_site_years_multi = sum(table(pop_year) >= 2), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("job", "part")) %>%
  left_join(informed_of("pop_year_event") %>% rename(event_sd_informed = informed),
            by = c("job", "part"))

if (nrow(season_summary) > 0) season_summary %>%
  transmute(species = species_label(taxon_capture), part, summary, n_events, n_site_years_multi,
            event_sd_informed,
            value = fmt_ci(value_median, value_lower_95, value_upper_95),
            pd = round(value_pd, 3), support = value_support) %>%
  arrange(part, species, summary)

season_curves = season_curve_draws(season_units, get_event_contrasts)
# facets marked when the event contrast sd is mostly prior (curves then flat by design)
event_sd_note = informed_of("pop_year_event") %>%
  filter(!informed) %>%
  transmute(job, part, note = "\n(event sd mostly prior)")
plot_season_curves = function(part_name) {
  plot_curves(season_curves, season_units %>% mutate(point_value = contrast_median), part_name,
              y_label = paste0(part_name, " contrast"),
              subtitle = paste0(part_name, ": co-sampled event medians (points) and per-draw seasonal smooths ",
                                "(100 draws, natural spline 3 df, pooled across site-years)"),
              facet_note = event_sd_note %>% filter(part == part_name) %>% select(job, note))
}

p_season_prev = plot_season_curves("prevalence")
p_season_load = plot_season_curves("load")
p_season_prev
p_season_load

# ---- the contrast across years within sites (tiers A and B, co-sampled site-years) ----
# swings between years without a drift are what the site-year contrast sd measures (Q3)
year_units = group_contrasts %>%
  filter(variant == "main", level == "pop_year", co_sampled)

year_draws = year_pattern_draws(year_units, function(job, part) unit_draws(job, part, "pop_year"))
year_summary = summarise_unit_draws(year_draws, c("slope_within", "slope_pooled"))
if (nrow(year_summary) > 0) year_summary = year_summary %>%
  left_join(year_units %>%
              group_by(job, part) %>%
              summarise(n_site_years = n(), n_years = n_distinct(year),
                        n_sites_multi = sum(table(population) >= 2), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("job", "part")) %>%
  left_join(informed_of("pop_year") %>% rename(site_year_sd_informed = informed),
            by = c("job", "part"))

if (nrow(year_summary) > 0) year_summary %>%
  transmute(species = species_label(taxon_capture), part, summary, n_site_years, n_years,
            n_sites_multi, site_year_sd_informed,
            value = fmt_ci(value_median, value_lower_95, value_upper_95),
            pd = round(value_pd, 3), support = value_support) %>%
  arrange(part, species, summary)

```

## Absolute patterns: overall infection through the season and years (item 4; supplement)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 14

# the same per-draw summaries for the event and site-year INTERCEPTS: overall infection (the
# midpoint of the two stages), not the gap. intercepts are informed by every unit, so far more
# events count than for the contrast, in every tier (D included).
# units: "observed" events / site-years, >= 5 swabs (prevalence) or >= 3 positive swabs (load),
# not co-sampled ones. the midpoint avoids predicting a stage where it was not swabbed.
# scales: slopes and late - early on the model scale (logit prevalence, log load among
# positives); curves and points back-transformed to prevalence and median load among positives.
# caveats as above (no seasonal / year term, pooled comparisons mix in sampling timing), plus:
# absolute levels are within-species only (labs differ in sensitivity), and the midpoint is not a
# population average weighted by the stages present.
min_swabs_abs = 5
min_pos_abs = 3

observed_units = function(level_name) {
  group_intercepts %>%
    filter(variant == "main", level == level_name) %>%
    mutate(n_swabs = n_adult + n_subadult, n_pos = n_pos_adult + n_pos_subadult) %>%
    filter(if_else(part == "prevalence", n_swabs >= min_swabs_abs, n_pos >= min_pos_abs))
}

# within the season
abs_season_units = observed_units("pop_year_event") %>% add_season_day()
get_event_intercepts = function(job, part) int_unit_draws(job, part, "pop_year_event")

abs_season_draws = season_pattern_draws(abs_season_units, get_event_intercepts)
abs_season_summary = summarise_unit_draws(abs_season_draws, c("slope_within", "slope_pooled", "late_minus_early"))
if (nrow(abs_season_summary) > 0) abs_season_summary = abs_season_summary %>%
  left_join(abs_season_units %>%
              group_by(job, part) %>%
              summarise(n_events = n(),
                        n_site_years_multi = sum(table(pop_year) >= 2), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("job", "part"))

if (nrow(abs_season_summary) > 0) abs_season_summary %>%
  transmute(species = species_label(taxon_capture), part, summary, n_events, n_site_years_multi,
            value = fmt_ci(value_median, value_lower_95, value_upper_95),
            pd = round(value_pd, 3), support = value_support) %>%
  arrange(part, species, summary)

# curves on readable scales: prevalence = plogis(-hu intercept); median load among positives =
# exp(mu intercept), on a log axis
abs_curves = bind_rows(
  season_curve_draws(abs_season_units %>% filter(part == "prevalence"), get_event_intercepts,
                     transform = plogis),
  season_curve_draws(abs_season_units %>% filter(part == "load"), get_event_intercepts,
                     transform = exp))
abs_points = abs_season_units %>%
  mutate(point_value = if_else(part == "prevalence", plogis(intercept_median), exp(intercept_median)))

p_abs_season_prev = plot_curves(abs_curves, abs_points, "prevalence",
                                y_label = "prevalence (midpoint of the two stages)",
                                subtitle = paste0("prevalence: observed event intercepts (points, >= ", min_swabs_abs,
                                                  " swabs) and per-draw seasonal smooths (100 draws)"),
                                y_scale = scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent), zero_line = FALSE)
p_abs_season_load = plot_curves(abs_curves, abs_points, "load",
                                y_label = "median load density among positives (midpoint)",
                                subtitle = paste0("load: observed event intercepts (points, >= ", min_pos_abs,
                                                  " positives) and per-draw seasonal smooths (100 draws)"),
                                y_scale = scale_y_log10(), zero_line = FALSE)
p_abs_season_prev
p_abs_season_load

# across years within sites
abs_year_units = observed_units("pop_year")
abs_year_draws = year_pattern_draws(abs_year_units, function(job, part) int_unit_draws(job, part, "pop_year"))
abs_year_summary = summarise_unit_draws(abs_year_draws, c("slope_within", "slope_pooled"))
if (nrow(abs_year_summary) > 0) abs_year_summary = abs_year_summary %>%
  left_join(abs_year_units %>%
              group_by(job, part) %>%
              summarise(n_site_years = n(), n_years = n_distinct(year),
                        n_sites_multi = sum(table(population) >= 2), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("job", "part"))

if (nrow(abs_year_summary) > 0) abs_year_summary %>%
  transmute(species = species_label(taxon_capture), part, summary, n_site_years, n_years, n_sites_multi,
            value = fmt_ci(value_median, value_lower_95, value_upper_95),
            pd = round(value_pd, 3), support = value_support) %>%
  arrange(part, species, summary)

```

# Consistency checks

## Against the unified model (m11g)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10

# m11g species x stage linear predictors (hu logit, mu) at each species' median subadult weather,
# from 03_size_bd_unified_analysis.qmd. the contrast does not depend on the weather values (weather
# slopes do not vary by stage). differences are expected: m11g pools species, includes weather and
# climate zones, and has no event level; the question is whether the two agree in sign and rough
# size. load contrasts only for jobs with a load stage term (m11g's would rest on the prior).
m11g_draws = read_parquet(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "unified_03_b_spp_lss_draws.parquet"))

m11g_contrast = m11g_draws %>%
  select(taxon_capture, life_stage_simple, .draw, hu, mu) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = life_stage_simple, values_from = c(hu, mu)) %>%
  transmute(taxon_capture, .draw,
            prevalence = -(hu_subadult - hu_adult),
            load = mu_subadult - mu_adult) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(prevalence, load), names_to = "part", values_to = "m11g")

m11g_agg = f_draw_agg(m11g_contrast, c("taxon_capture", "part"), "m11g")

consistency_m11g = species_summary %>%
  filter(variant == "main") %>%
  select(taxon_capture, part, tier, fit_ok, contrast_median, contrast_lower_95, contrast_upper_95,
         contrast_support) %>%
  inner_join(m11g_agg %>% select(taxon_capture, part, m11g_median, m11g_lower_95, m11g_upper_95, m11g_support),
             by = c("taxon_capture", "part")) %>%
  mutate(same_sign = sign(contrast_median) == sign(m11g_median),
         part = factor(part, levels = c("prevalence", "load")))

p_consistency_m11g = ggplot(consistency_m11g, aes(x = m11g_median, y = contrast_median, color = tier)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey85") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = contrast_lower_95, ymax = contrast_upper_95), width = 0, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = m11g_lower_95, xmax = m11g_upper_95), width = 0, alpha = 0.5, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(aes(alpha = fit_ok), size = 2) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.35), guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = tier_colors) +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "m11g contrast (median, 95%)", y = "contrast model (median, 95%)",
       subtitle = "dashed = 1:1") +
  theme_classic()

p_consistency_m11g

# disagreements in sign, or support in one model only
consistency_m11g %>%
  filter(!same_sign | contrast_support != m11g_support) %>%
  transmute(species = species_label(taxon_capture), part, tier,
            contrast = fmt_ci(contrast_median, contrast_lower_95, contrast_upper_95), contrast_support,
            m11g = fmt_ci(m11g_median, m11g_lower_95, m11g_upper_95), m11g_support)

```

## A. canorus: tier C (main) vs tier A (sensitivity)
```{r}
# does giving canorus the full tier A structure change its mean contrast, or its site-level
# variation? and are the extra (site-year, event) contrast sds informed at all?
canorus_jobs = jobs_fit %>% filter(taxon_capture == "anaxyrus_canorus") %>% pull(job)

(peace = species_summary %>%
  filter(job %in% canorus_jobs) %>%
  transmute(variant, part, tier, fit_ok,
            contrast = fmt_ci(contrast_median, contrast_lower_95, contrast_upper_95),
            support = contrast_support))

(hope = level_summary %>%
  filter(job %in% canorus_jobs) %>%
  left_join(jobs_fit %>% select(job, variant), by = "job") %>%
  transmute(variant, part, level = level_labels[as.character(level)],
            sd = fmt_ci(sd_median, sd_lower_95, sd_upper_95),
            contraction = round(contraction, 2),
            sign_consistency = round(sign_consistency_median, 2)) %>%
  arrange(part, level, variant))

```

## Against the seasonal models (optional)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10

# the seasonal models' window-mean contrast (the average subadult - adult difference over the
# co-sampled part of the season, or the sampled window) against this mean contrast. same scales.
# only where both fits passed the convergence flag. skipped if 03_season_all_species_analysis.Rmd
# has not been run.
season_file = here("size_bd_season", "intermediates", "03_all_contrast_summary.csv")

if (file.exists(season_file)) {
  consistency_season = read_csv(season_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(fit_ok) %>%
    transmute(taxon_capture, part = metric, window,
              season_median = window_mean_median, season_lower_95 = window_mean_lower_95,
              season_upper_95 = window_mean_upper_95) %>%
    inner_join(species_summary %>%
                 filter(variant == "main", fit_ok) %>%
                 select(taxon_capture, part, tier, contrast_median, contrast_lower_95, contrast_upper_95),
               by = c("taxon_capture", "part")) %>%
    mutate(part = factor(part, levels = c("prevalence", "load")))

  p_consistency_season = ggplot(consistency_season, aes(x = season_median, y = contrast_median, color = tier)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = contrast_lower_95, ymax = contrast_upper_95), width = 0, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = season_lower_95, xmax = season_upper_95), width = 0, alpha = 0.5, orientation = "y") +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = tier_colors) +
    facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free") +
    labs(x = "seasonal model window-mean contrast (median, 95%)", y = "contrast model (median, 95%)",
         subtitle = "species where both fits converged; dashed = 1:1") +
    theme_classic()
  p_consistency_season
} else {
  consistency_season = NULL
  p_consistency_season = NULL
  message("no seasonal summary found (", season_file, "): skipped")
}

```

# Export
```{r}
# for stage 2:
#   species_summary  one row per job x part: mean contrast (f_draw_agg columns), typical-site
#                    effect, per-level sd / contraction / sign consistency / share / correlation,
#                    tier, flags, fit_ok (species-level models)
#                    and each stage's level at a typical site (within-species context)
#   level_summary    the same per level, long, with the intercept sd, the contrast / intercept
#                    sd ratio and same-level intercept share
#   group_intercepts overall infection per site, site-year and event (all parts and tiers)
#   group_contrasts  one row per job x part x group (site, site-year, event): contrast mean / sd /
#                    quantiles, n per stage, co-sampled flag, population / year / event dates for
#                    joining climate. mean + sd supports contrast | se(sd) in brms
#   draws            1000 draws of mean contrasts, contrast sds and population contrasts (long:
#                    quantity, level, group_id, .draw, value), for repeated stage 2 fits
level_summary_out = level_summary %>%
  mutate(level = as.character(level)) %>%
  left_join(job_info %>% select(job, taxon_capture, variant, tier_hu, tier_mu), by = "job")

# local intermediates
write_csv(species_summary, file.path(intermediates_dir, "03_contrast_species_summary.csv"))

write_csv(year_summary, file.path(intermediates_dir, "03_contrast_year_summary.csv"))
```
